evidences.title: Hungary curbs political freedoms to fight terrorism
evidences.content:
BUDAPEST, Hungary  Hungarys parliament passed a constitutional amendment Tuesday that allowsthe government to limit social media and the public's right to assemble in a terrorist emergency.

The measure, passed 153-3 with one abstention, lets parliament declare a state of emergency for up to 15 days and use military forces inside the country in the event of aterrorist threat or attack.

Hungary has not had a terrorist attack, but the government raised its terror alert level after the Brussels suicide bombing attacks in March.

Opposition parties and civil liberties groups said Prime Minister Viktor Orban, already criticizedfor weakening the constitution to seize more power, could misuse the measure.

Socialist Party President Jozsef Tobias said the amendment was really about the governments ambitions of power, the Associated Press reported.Amnesty International has called the measure an open attack on human rights that gives the government sweeping powers that could alsostifle opposing views.

Hungary declares state of emergency amid migrant crisis

The move comes less than two weeks after a top U.S. diplomat for human rightswarned Hungary against using terrorist threats as a reason to crack down on political freedoms.

We have seen how demagogues can exploit difficult moments for political gain by playing on our worst human impulses and targeting constitutional rights and institutions designed to limit the power of those impulses, Undersecretary of State Sarah Sewall said in a speech to the Hungarian Journalists Association on May 26. Left unchecked, these forces can erode democracy and open the door to all manner of abuse and exploitation.

Orbans spokesman, Zoltan Kovacs, told USA TODAY that the change is mild in comparison to what is available to authorities in France or the United States, where you have really strict rules for dealing with terrorism.

The U.S. Patriot Act, passed after the Sept. 11, 2001, terrorist attacks expanded the government's power tomonitor phone and email communications andbank records of Americans.

Francedeclared a state of emergency Nov. 15, two days after multiple terrorist attacks in Paris killed 130 people, and it is still in place, Kovacs said.We would like less at our disposal than the European governments have, he said.

Last year, Orban ordered security officials to erect a razor-wire fence along Hungarys border with Serbia to block a flood of migrants, includingSyrian warrefugees seeking safetyin northern Europe.The European Commission Against Racism and Intolerance criticized thatmove as pandering to a growing anti-immigrant backlash inHungary.

Sewall said bigoted and xenophobic rhetoric is on the rise in both the United Statesand Hungary. "We must answer these moments of challenge by holding fast to coredemocratic values and institutions," she said.

Kovacs saidlistening and addressing voters fears is good governance.Its listening to the voice of the people, he said. If they feel something is wrong, like the immigration crisis, then you have to deal with it in a proper way.
